reason: Commit 8cf03fc closes the ordinary sighted pile_limit transaction through valid startup parsing, movement, every count word, the heavy-wish floor-drop prerequisite, and carrying-capacity rendering. Every retained exclusion refuses before observable mutation.

boundary.startingEvent: A sighted walking hero with autopickup disabled takes one ordinary step onto a ROOM or CORR square holding at least two objects, with pile_limit greater than zero and no greater than the object count.
boundary.endingEvent: The game has stopped any run, displayed the source-selected two, a few, several, or many objects message, preserved the pile, and reached the next command input.
boundary.validInputs: Ordinary ROOM and CORR destinations; safe piles of 2, 3-4, 5-9, and at least 10 objects; source-valid pile_limit spellings whose positive value triggers skipping. pile_limit:0 and a non-triggering threshold are negative controls that retain the already-ported menu path.
boundary.observables: Option state, hero position and run stop, object-chain state, random-number log, messages, complete terminal screens and attributes, cursors, and persisted state through the next command input.
boundary.exclusions: Single objects; autopickup and picked_some/another/more wording; blind or swallowed heroes; cockatrice handling; decorated or mention_decor destinations; traps, visible regions, engravings, inaccessible liquids, and behavior after the next command input.

candidateListMethod.upstreamEntryPoints: options.c optfn_pile_limit(), pickup.c pickup() and check_here(), and invent.c look_here() from skip_objects assignment through the ordinary count arm.
candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: optlist.h pile_limit metadata and its default PILE_LIMIT_DFLT value; count partitions at 2, 5, and 10; ROOM and CORR destination families.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: Trace option parsing through startup flags, domove/spoteffects into pickup/check_here, then look_here through the first observable message and return, including read_engr_at ordering and nomul(0).
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: Search options.js, hack.js, pickup.js, and invent.js for pile_limit, skipped-pile, object-pile size, object naming, decoration, trap, region, engraving, liquid, blindness, cockatrice, and autopickup stops.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: The fixed session census currently aborts after seed0030 advances beyond this goal to the later dosounds has_shop boundary; a read-only per-session scan found no development session presently first-stopped at either remaining pile slice. A 100,000-seed D:1 census found 14 clean five-node piles and no clean ten-node pile. Seven 1,000-seed starting-pet scans through 100 turns added at most two nodes and found no pet-grown five- or ten-node pile, so the ten-node live case requires an already-valid command path that creates floor objects.

entries.reachability: OPTIONS can set pile_limit explicitly, omit its value, or negate it before the first move; look_here reads the resulting flag before any pile output.
entries.effects: Set the integer threshold using C atoi/default/negation and negative-value fallback semantics.
entries.evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/options.c optfn_pile_limit() and include/optlist.h pile_limit entry; current generic JS compound parsing preserves strings and treats a bare spelling as boolean true.
entries.remaining: Verified valid numeric, signed, zero, negative, nonnumeric, empty-negation, and missing-positive-value behavior against optfn_pile_limit() and fresh startup.

entries.reachability: preflightDomoveDestination sees a ROOM or CORR object chain before domove, while flags.pickup is false.
entries.effects: Permit a pile of any count to proceed only when the skip condition is true; retain the two-to-four menu gate when it is false and preserve all existing exclusions.
entries.evidence: Current preflight rejects counts above four before testing pile_limit and rejects every true skip as skipped-pile count.
entries.remaining: Verified ordinary triggering piles at counts 2, 3, 5, and 10 plus non-triggering controls through the movement consumer.

entries.effects: Stop an active run with nomul(0), flush, and pass the exact object count to look_here.

entries.remaining: Verified unchanged nomul(), flush, count, and look_here() ordering in the six-segment fresh differential.

entries.reachability: look_here receives obj_cnt at least two and 0 < pile_limit <= obj_cnt on an otherwise ordinary square.
entries.effects: Read engraving in source order, then emit two for count 2, a few for 3-4, several for 5-9, or many for at least 10, without naming or modifying objects.
entries.evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/invent.c look_here() skip_objects branch at the count message arm; JS currently throws at both the preflight and look_here seams.
entries.remaining: Verified two, a few, several, and many through the next prompt with unchanged object identity, ownership, and dknown state.

entries.candidate: ordinary heavy-wish drop prerequisite for the ten-node live case
entries.reachability: A debug hero wishes for a non-blocking, non-merging object whose weight raises near_capacity, so invent.c hold_another_object() takes drop_it and do.c dropx()/dropy()/dropz() places it on the hero's ordinary ROOM or CORR square. Repeating the command creates the source-valid ten-node pile that the movement boundary consumes.
entries.owner: js/invent.js hold_another_object() and js/do.js dropx(), dropy(), and dropz()
entries.effects: Undo any inventory merge when required, print the wish drop line, unlink the object from inventory, place and stack it on ordinary ground, redraw the hero square, and return to the command prompt without admitting shipping, altar, shop, swallowed, impact, liquid, trap, worn-slot, or other drop branches.
entries.evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/invent.c hold_another_object() drop_it and nethack-c/upstream/src/do.c dropx(), dropy(), and dropz(); the recorder patches expose no state-injection hook, a 100,000-seed natural census found no clean ten-node pile, and a 7,000-seed pet scan found no credible accumulation route.
entries.remaining: Verified three carried and ten dropped nonmerging heavy iron balls, both floor-chain indexes, the wish-tail RNG draw, drop output, redraw, exclusions, and the final many transaction against C.

entries.candidate: carrying-capacity status field exposed by wish preloading

entries.owner: js/display.js tty status layout port of botl.c and windows.c
entries.effects: Render the source carrying-capacity word and its spacing on every status refresh while the hero is burdened or stressed, preserving source field order and the existing width fit.
entries.evidence: The first expanded C/JavaScript differential mismatch is the Burdened/Stressed status cell while preloading the third iron ball; nethack-c/upstream/src/botl.c fills BL_CAP and nethack-c/upstream/src/windows.c orders it after BL_HUNGER.
entries.remaining: Verified two- and three-row BL_CAP field order, source alignment, and exact-width shortening boundaries in focused tests and the fresh heavy-wish transaction.

sourceReview: Complete at 8cf03fc11dcb43810468d73666676982740ccd34: traced every reachable branch and helper from valid startup pile_limit parsing through movement, pickup/check_here, look_here, the ordinary heavy-wish drop prerequisite, and BL_CAP rendering against upstream C. The trace covered state and PRNG order, both floor-object indexes, terminal output, and every retained fail-closed exclusion. Six fresh segments matched 21,419 PRNG calls and 209 complete screens/cursors; the retained two-segment pile-window matrix matched 8,062 calls and 12 screens/cursors.
